# VIBE CODING — CINEMATIC EXPERIMENT · EXAMINATION REPORT
**Subject:** "The Lantern Archive of Velmar" — generated by Google AI Studio Build (Gemini 4 Neon) from the captain's sanitized fictional spec; single generation **10m 04s** (per the build record).
**Export examined:** `~/workspace/research_notes/aistudio-exports/lantern-archive-source.zip` (154,898 B), extracted unmodified to `living-universe/vibe-experiment-exam/src/`. The zip was never altered.
**Method:** full source read · safety grep sweep · local install/build · static serve of the production build · two puppeteer sessions (desktop 1280×800, mobile 375×667) driven through the real UI · pixel-difference measurements · the examiner's own visual read of 12 captured frames (kept in `vibe-experiment-exam/shots/`).
**Examiner's verdict, up front:** this is a genuinely capable piece of generated software — **7 of 8 spec requirements PASS, 1 PARTIAL** — with three precise factory-test findings (install leg fails as-shipped · one external network call · template baggage). **No blanket PASS is issued for the experiment as a whole**, because req 8 is partial and the Stranger Test's clean-install leg fails; what the evidence *does* carry is stated requirement by requirement below.

---

## 1 · ARCHITECTURE

**Inventory (19 files, 152,228 B uncompressed; 4,513 lines total incl. config):**

| File | Lines | Bytes | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/engine/archiveRenderer.ts` | 1,821 | 59,621 | The entire painterly canvas renderer (monolith) |
| `src/components/ArchiveCanvas.tsx` | 703 | 22,047 | The world engine: rAF loop, locomotion, owl AI, doors, input |
| `src/components/StarCompassModal.tsx` | 595 | 26,097 | Parchment unroll + manifestation + separation UI |
| `src/components/StarCompassSVG.tsx` | 446 | 13,251 | Layered SVG drawings of the compass + its 5 parts |
| `src/engine/worldGeometry.ts` | 251 | 7,433 | Projection, collision, waypoint routing |
| `src/types/archive.ts` | 123 | 2,356 | State types for every actor/system |
| `src/App.tsx` | 115 | 5,307 | Shell: header, proximity prompt, panel + modal mounting |
| `src/data/archiveData.ts` | 95 | 3,274 | Lore, compass parts, price — as data |
| `src/components/DoorChamberPanel.tsx` | 87 | 3,551 | Door chamber lore panel |
| `src/index.css` | 137 | 3,458 | Tailwind 4 + parchment/scroll styling + spin keyframes |
| `index.html`, `src/main.tsx`, configs | — | — | Vite + React 19 + TS shell |

**Build shape:** Vite 8 + React 19 + TypeScript (strict `tsc --noEmit` passes clean). **No server exists in the export** despite `express`/`dotenv`/`@google/genai` being declared dependencies and `metadata.json` claiming `MAJOR_CAPABILITY_SERVER_SIDE_GEMINI_API` — the AI Studio full-stack template's skeleton shipped around a purely client-side app (see §2).

**How each system is implemented:**
- **Locomotion** (`ArchiveCanvas.tsx` §2 of the loop): velocity model with exponential accel/decel blending (rate 7.5/8.5), max speeds 0.42/0.31 world-units/s, arrival slowdown inside 0.14 units, `walkPhase` advanced from speed, legs settle to a neutral stance at rest, facing flips on real horizontal velocity with a smoothed `visualFacing`. Input: click/tap waypoints **and** WASD/arrows, plus E/Enter/Space to work a near door.
- **Following** (§3): the owl targets a point behind the traveler's facing (−0.125x, +0.032z), speed scales with distance (0.14 + 1.45·d, capped 0.46), wing phase + hop height while moving, and at rest: head look-around on a randomized timer (5 target angles), blink cycle (0.13s closed / 2.4–5.8s open), facing settles toward the traveler.
- **Depth** (`worldGeometry.ts` + `archiveRenderer.ts`): a true perspective projection — `zPersp = 1/(1.68 − 0.68z)`, screen y and actor scale derived from it, with an exact inverse (`screenToWorld`) for click mapping. The renderer paints in layers: background plane (parallax 0.55) → back wall → perspective floor → side walls/doors → **depth-sorted drawables** (table z 0.57, front shelves 0.84, traveler/owl at their own z — painter's algorithm, so actors occlude correctly) → chandelier → dust (per-mote parallax 0.45–1.2 by depth) → foreground piers (parallax 1.38).
- **Collision** (`worldGeometry.ts`): circle-vs-AABB resolution against 5 named obstacle boxes + floor bounds, two passes, run **every frame for both actors**. Routing: `computeWaypoints` tests the straight segment against the (padded) central table and, if blocked, builds left/right detours and picks the shorter — routing intelligence covers the table; the shelves are handled by resolution only.
- **Manifestation state**: *not* a formal state machine — three booleans in `StarCompassModal.tsx` (`unrolled` at 45ms, `manifested` at 420ms, `separated` toggled), CSS transitions doing the visual work, a separate particle canvas (gold particles, own rAF) behind the parchment. Simpler than our house state machine, and it works; it is also less strict (no skip-proofing, no sequence token).
- **Data-driven or hard-coded?** **Split verdict.** Content is data: lore, the 5 compass parts (name/index/description/material/radial offset/label side), the price card (`archiveData.ts`), obstacle boxes and door definitions are typed data structures. The *world itself* is hard-coded: the hall exists only as ~1,800 lines of imperative canvas draw calls in one file — there is no scene schema, no route graph, no data a second room could be authored from. A second product could be data; a second *place* could not.

## 2 · SAFETY SWEEP (factory test cards)

- **Keys/secrets in source: NONE.** Full grep for key patterns, `api_key`, `secret`, `password`, `token`: the only hit is the fictional price string "180 in archive tokens". `.env.example` contains placeholders only (`GEMINI_API_KEY=` with a "MY_…" placeholder value, `APP_URL="MY_APP_URL"`).
- **Key custody: PASS.** No key is embedded, requested, or referenced by any code path. `@google/genai` is declared in `package.json` but **never imported anywhere** in the source.
- **Network calls in app code: NONE** — no `fetch(`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`, or `axios` anywhere.
- **Zero-call proof: PASS for application logic, FAIL for strict offline purity.** The one external reference is `index.html` loading **Google Fonts** CSS. Proven consequence-free here: in this sandbox the font request failed (`ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED`) and the app still ran completely — every test in §3 was executed with fonts blocked. But a strict zero-call gate counts it: the export is not network-silent as shipped.
- **Clean-install leg (Stranger Test): FAIL as-shipped.** A plain `npm install` errors with ERESOLVE: `package.json` pins `esbuild ^0.25.0` while its own `vite ^8.3.0` requires peer `esbuild ^0.27 || ^0.28`. `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` succeeds (181 packages), after which `npm run build` succeeds (dist JS 290.88 kB / gzip 91.00 kB · CSS 35.21 kB / gzip 7.41 kB) and `tsc --noEmit` is clean. A stranger following the README hits the wall on step 1.
- **Template baggage (not defects, but not house property either):** unused `express`, `dotenv`, `@google/genai` dependencies; `metadata.json`'s server-side-Gemini capability claim with no server present; a README that points at AI Studio deployment.

## 3 · LOCAL RUN — MEASURED EVIDENCE (puppeteer, production build, local serve)

- **(a) Walk + follow — VERIFIED.** Clicked floor at (329,685): frame at +0.8s shows the traveler mid-stride ~280px west of his start, facing his travel direction, **the owl displaced behind him in wing-spread hop pose** (examiner's visual read, `shots/d1-midwalk.png`). Floor-band pixel change start→arrival: **7.31%**. Two frames 1.5s apart *after* arrival: **0.20%** changed — both figures at rest (the owl pauses when the traveler pauses), only environmental shimmer remains.
- **(b) DOOR TEST (the one the build run never verified) — VERIFIED END-TO-END.** Clicked the **Vault** door's screen position (1140,450) from across the hall: the traveler walked to the door's stand point, the door opened on arrival, and the chamber panel mounted — DOM-confirmed "The Vault / Reliquary Strongroom" after **2.0s** of polling (`shots/d6-vault-door.png`; the panel only mounts from the `onDoorOpened` callback, which fires only when the door's open state flips). Proximity glow, the bottom "Open Vault" prompt, and closing/re-closing are all in the same verified code path; a mid-swing leaf frame was not captured (the swing itself is an eased `openAmount` 0→1 driving a hinged-leaf render in `drawSideWallsAndDoors`).
- **(c) COLLISION TEST — VERIFIED, twice.** (i) From west of the table, clicked *north* of it (640,455): the +1.3s frame shows the traveler at the table's **south-west corner heading around its west end** — the waypoint detour, not a straight line through the box (`shots/d3-midroute-around-table.png`; the same frame catches a table book mid-page-turn). (ii) Clicked **inside** the table's screen area (640,544): the target was resolved out of the box and the traveler ended at the table's **north face, correctly occluded by the table** (hood visible above its far edge, `shots/d5-click-inside-table.png`). At no sampled moment does either actor overlap an obstacle.
- **(d) MOBILE 375×667 — scrubber VERIFIED, with a blemish.** Tap-to-walk works (with the mobile camera follow-pan). In the modal, `#mobile-layer-scrubber` exists and is visible; stepping via the "04" index button moved the range value 0→3 and the active part to **Needle Assembly** (`shots/m2–m3`). **Blemish:** the manifestation modal is taller than the 667px viewport — at first paint the Reassemble button is clipped and the price card sits below the fold (reachable by scrolling the modal, not visible). Everything functions; the first screenful is cut.
- **(e) Continuous animation — VERIFIED.** Two frames 2.0s apart at rest: full-frame **0.29%** of pixels changed above threshold; the hanging-lamp crop **3.68%** (sway + flicker); the chandelier's swung position is visibly different between `d0` and `d1`; a book page is caught mid-turn in `d3`. In code the environmental block (96 dust motes, 3 turning books, ripples) is step 1 of the loop — unconditional, running behind the door panel and the modal alike.
- **(f) Page errors — ZERO.** No `pageerror` and no console error from app code in either session. The only failed requests: the sandbox-blocked Google Fonts CSS (see §2) and `favicon.ico` 404.
- **Reduced motion (house standard, beyond the spec):** one `prefers-reduced-motion` rule exists — it stills the compass spin in the modal. The world loop does not honor it. Recorded as a gap against house law, not against the 8 requirements.
- **Performance note:** no formal FPS measurement was taken (headless environment caveat applies, per house law on motion evidence); the rAF loop advanced smoothly enough for every timed behavior above to land on schedule.

## 4 · THE EIGHT REQUIREMENTS — SCORED

| # | Requirement | Grade | Evidence in one line |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Navigable environment, genuine spatial depth | **PASS** | Real perspective projection + inverse mapping, parallax planes 0.55/1.38, depth-sorted actors; click + keyboard navigation both driven |
| 2 | Avatar locomotion | **PASS** | Accel/decel velocity model, procedural leg swing, facing, arrival slowdown, settle — observed moving and arriving |
| 3 | Companion following | **PASS** | Owl observed trailing mid-walk in hop pose, rests beside the traveler (settle diff 0.20%), look-around + blink systems in code |
| 4 | Doors + interactions + collision | **PASS** | Vault door: walk-to → open → chamber panel, DOM-proven in 2.0s; collision detour + inside-click resolution both observed; actors never overlap obstacles |
| 5 | Continuous environmental animation | **PASS** | Lamp crop 3.68% px / 2s at rest, page-turn caught live, dust in every frame; the loop's environment block is unconditional |
| 6 | Parchment unroll + manifestation | **PASS** | Unrolled parchment with rollers, golden particle canvas, rotating manifested compass (`shots/d7`); summon works from header button and the table-scroll hit-box |
| 7 | Separation / reassembly + labels + price + closed purchasing | **PASS** | All 5 part labels DOM-verified with leader lines + dots (`shots/d8`); reassembly changed 11.79% of stage pixels back; price string exact; "Purchasing closed" button present and `disabled` (DOM-verified) |
| 8 | Responsive desktop + mobile controls | **PARTIAL** | Desktop complete; mobile tap-walk, camera pan and scrubber all work — but the modal overflows the 375×667 first screenful (toggle clipped, price card below the fold), and the radial stage exists only ≥1024px |

**Experiment total: 7 PASS · 1 PARTIAL · 0 FAIL** — and the §2 findings stand beside the score: the export does not pass the house's clean-install or strict zero-call legs as shipped.

## 5 · COMPARISON — GENERATED vs HAND-BUILT (prototype journey, pass 2 + fix pass, blind-verified 9/9)

| Axis | AI Studio Build (generated) | Prototype journey (hand-built) |
|---|---|---|
| **Construction time** | **10m 04s** single generation from one prompt (+ founder walk/export handling) | ~3 crew-hours across 5 relay seats in one evening (pass 1 → pass 2 → critic → fix pass → blind verify) + captain verification |
| **Code size** | 4,399 lines of app code (TS/TSX/CSS/HTML), ~148 KB; built bundle 290.9 kB JS (91.0 gzip) | 1,375 lines hand-written (journey.js 918 + HTML 218 + CSS 239), ~74 KB — *plus* shared house assets it stands on (Solnik rig, Job films, town stills) not counted in that figure |
| 1 · Depth/environment | **Generated better** — true geometric projection, one coherent self-drawn room | Data-modeled depth over real film/stills; less geometric, but carries *real cinema* (Job 5's film plays in its Library) |
| 2 · Locomotion | **Generated slightly better** — velocity model + keyboard + click in one system | Tap-to-walk only; but drives the real articulated Solnik rig |
| 3 · Companion | Even — a complete self-contained follow/look/blink owl | Even — the actual Solnik, house rig, follow verified by the blind seat |
| 4 · Doors + collision | **Generated clearly better** — proximity doors, walk-to-open, real collision + routing | Portal overlay; **no collision (defect D-2, carried knowingly)** |
| 5 · Continuous life | Even — code-animated environment, never pauses | Even — film + CSS life loops, verified ungated during manifestation |
| 6 · Manifestation | **Generated slightly better** presentation (unroll + particles + rotation) | Wired to *real* products (Mint, Keeper) — generated one's product is fictional |
| 7 · Separation | Even — radial + scrubber, polished | Even — same pattern through **one engine for any product**, with verbatim listing data |
| 8 · Responsive | Partial — modal overflows 375×667 | **Hand-built better** — 375px behavior incl. the hidden-state law, blind-verified after the fix pass |
| Verification posture | Arrived UNVERIFIED; this report is its first independent examination | Full Relay circuit closed: builder → critic → improver → blind verifier, unanimous |

**Honest summary of the comparison:** on *mechanism breadth per hour*, the generated build is remarkable — it produced, in ten minutes, working versions of three things our hand-built line either simplified (collision) or had not yet reached (proximity doors). On *truth and trust* — real products, verbatim data, a verified hidden-state law, reduced-motion honor, an engine that any product or place can be authored into — the hand-built line remains ahead. The generated world is a brilliant single room; the house system is a poorer-looking *factory for worlds*.

## 6 · INTEGRATION JUDGMENT (Generator-Neutral: adopt mechanisms, never raw code trust)

**WORTH ADOPTING — re-implemented/verified in our tree:**
1. **`worldGeometry.ts` wholesale as a mechanism** — perspective projection + exact inverse, circle-vs-AABB resolution, and table-detour waypoint routing. This *closes our own D-2*: the World Engine seat (construction wave 1) explicitly shipped without collision. Highest-value adoption in the export.
2. **The door pattern** — proximity radius + glow lerp + *walk-to-stand-point, then open on arrival* (`pendingDoorId`) + chamber panel. A reusable interaction pattern for World Engine doors/thresholds.
3. **The follow model** — offset-behind-facing anchor, distance-scaled follow speed, idle look-around/blink timers — as a *behavior reference* for the avatar-system companion (ours is rig-based; theirs is a clean, complete statement of the same behaviors).
4. **Depth-sorted painter's render list** — drawables sorted by z each frame; matches our spatial model's renderer interface and is a sound reference for the 2.5-D compositing renderer (Architecture v1.1).
5. **The mobile scrubber's index-button row** (01–05 jump buttons beside the range input) — a small, better detail than our scrubber's prev/next only.

**NOT ADOPTED:**
1. **The canvas monolith as a renderer** (1,821 lines, one hard-coded room) — our road is the film/2.5-D hybrid with scenes as data; this cannot author a second place.
2. **The boolean-timer manifestation state** — our Manifestation Engine's explicit, skip-proof state machine is strictly stronger; theirs stays a presentation reference only.
3. **All AI Studio template baggage** — the unused `@google/genai`/`express`/`dotenv` dependencies, the phantom server-side capability claim, the deploy-to-AI-Studio README path. None of it enters the house tree.
4. **The Google Fonts dependency** — house surfaces self-host their type; a world that must phone a font server fails our zero-call discipline.

**Standing of the experiment:** the founder's question — *how much of the actual cinematic software can Vibe Coding build?* — now has a measured answer: **most of one room's mechanisms, in minutes, at a quality that beats our hand-built prototype on doors, collision and locomotion breadth — and none of the civilization's load-bearing properties (data-authored places, real products, verified states, ownership-clean install) without the house's own engineering around it.** The methodology earns its place in the FVR-31 pipeline as a *mechanism foundry*: generate → examine → adopt mechanisms into verified house engines. That is a construction instrument, proven — inside the Relay, under the fences, exactly as registered.

— Examination seat (Relay), 2026-11-25 night. No deployment made. The captain files this report to the desk.
